cover.Transaction:: FY2024 debt, liquidity, and refinancing profile -- general corporate, no transaction pending
cover.Next maturity / launch:: FY2025 (within twelve months of 2024-06-30): 8,942 $mm of tagged near-term maturities (LongTermDebtCurrent 2,249 + commercial paper 6,693)
cover.Refresh cadence:: Annual, on Microsoft's Form 10-K (fiscal year ends 30 June)

source.name: Microsoft 2024 Form 10-K
source.notes: EBIT (us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss), NOT EBITDA. Microsoft tags no DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization concept in this fact set, so EBITDA cannot be derived from it. EBIT is used as a conservative lower bound: it understates EBITDA, which understates interest coverage and overstates leverage, so the case errs toward making Microsoft's credit look worse than it is, never better. FY2024 OperatingIncomeLoss = 109,433 $mm. Downside is the lowest of FY2024, FY2023, FY2022 (83,383 $mm).

source.name: Microsoft 2024 Form 10-K
source.notes: us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue at 2024-06-30 = 18,315 $mm. Strict cash and equivalents -- narrower than the liquidity figure on the refinancing sheet (75,543 $mm), which is cash AND short-term investments per the 10-K. Downside is the lowest of FY2024, FY2023, FY2022.

source.name: Microsoft 2024 Form 10-K
source.notes: us-gaap:CommercialPaper at 2024-06-30 = 6,693 $mm. Mapped to the template's 'revolver drawn' line because commercial paper is the short-term borrowing Microsoft actually had outstanding and is the balance that must be rolled within twelve months; Microsoft's revolving credit facility itself was undrawn. Labelled here so the line is not misread as revolver borrowings.

source.name: Microsoft 2024 Form 10-K
source.notes: Zero. Microsoft's XBRL debt facts disclose no term-loan instrument -- the entire long-term balance is tagged under LongTermDebt / LongTermDebtNoncurrent, consistent with a notes-and-leases capital structure. The template's $300mm term-loan default is a generic mid-cap placeholder and is removed.

source.name: Microsoft 2024 Form 10-K
source.notes: us-gaap:LongTermDebt at 2024-06-30 = 44,937 $mm, carried on the senior-notes line because Microsoft's long-term debt is senior unsecured notes. Downside is the highest of FY2024, FY2023, FY2022 (49,781 $mm) -- more debt is the adverse direction.

source.name: Microsoft 2024 Form 10-K
source.notes: Residual: disclosed total debt 67,127 - LongTermDebt 44,937 - CommercialPaper 6,693 = 15,497 $mm. Finance leases and other borrowings Microsoft does not tag separately in this fact set. Carrying it as the residual is what makes gross debt on the Capital Structure sheet tie EXACTLY to the disclosed total. Disclosed total debt of 67,127 $mm is BROADER than the XBRL LongTermDebt tag (44,937 $mm): it includes finance leases and other borrowings Microsoft reports outside that concept. Both figures are real and measure different things; the capital structure uses the broader disclosed total so gross debt ties to the filing.

source.name: Case driver (no tagged disclosure exists)
source.notes: Floating base rate. Not company data; it would come from a rates source (FRED), which is not reachable in this environment. It feeds only the term-loan line, which is zero for Microsoft, so it is inert here.

source.name: Case driver (no tagged disclosure exists)
source.notes: All-in cost of the commercial-paper balance. Microsoft does not tag a commercial-paper rate. Held as a driver -- and note the AGGREGATE it feeds is pinned: the senior-notes coupon is solved so total cash interest equals the disclosed InterestExpense of 2,935 $mm regardless of how this splits.

source.name: Case driver (no tagged disclosure exists)
source.notes: Term-loan spread. Inert: Microsoft has no term loan.

source.name: Microsoft 2024 Form 10-K
source.notes: Solved so Capital Structure cash interest equals the disclosed us-gaap:InterestExpense of 2,935 $mm for FY2024. The template charges both the senior-notes and other-debt lines at this rate, so coupon = (InterestExpense - CommercialPaper x revolver spread) / (LongTermDebt + other debt) = 0.043028. Per-instrument coupons are in the 10-K debt note as tabular HTML, not as tagged facts; the weighted burden is what is disclosed, and it is what is pinned.

refresh.trigger: Depth pass: full input accounting against recorded XBRL facts
refresh.what_changed: Rebuilt the case from Microsoft's recorded SEC XBRL facts. It previously carried four sourced cells out of 102 candidates (4.9%) with every other input left at a generic leveraged-mid-cap template default -- a $300mm term loan Microsoft does not have, a 5.5x leverage covenant it is not subject to, a 5.5% coupon. Capital structure now ties exactly to disclosed total debt, cash interest and weighted cost are solved to disclosed interest expense, and every remaining cell is a declared driver with a stated reason.
refresh.reviewer_notes: External historical case; human stakeholder approval remains pending. EBITDA is proxied by EBIT because Microsoft tags no D&A concept; the bias is conservative (understates coverage, overstates leverage).
refresh.next_check: On Microsoft's next Form 10-K, builder change, or annual review
